chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man had intercourse with his wife while he was making up the days of Ramadan.' He said, 'If he had intercourse with her before the 'Asr prayer, there is no penalty upon him; he fasts one day in its place. And if he did it after 'Asr, he fasts that day and feeds ten poor people. If he is unable to do so, he fasts three days as expiation for that.'

Muammad ibn al-Hasan said, 'There is no contradiction between the two reports because when the time for the two prayers is at the decline of the sun, except that Dhuhr is before 'Asr as we have established previously, it is permissible to describe what is before the decline as being before 'Asr due to the closeness between the two times, and to describe what is after 'Asr as being after the decline in the same way. And it is permissible to carry this narration if one determines the time and meaning within it to be obligatory, and the first case to be recommended.'

key_terms.زَوَالُ الشَّمْسِ: Decline of the sun (time when Dhuhr ends and 'Asr begins)
key_terms.قَضَاءُ رَمَضَانَ: Making up missed days of Ramadan fasting
key_terms.كَفَّارَة: Expiation or compensation for a religious violation

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking the fast of Ramadan due to intercourse before or after the Asr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār details the specific expiation (kaffarah) for breaking the Ramadan fast through intercourse, distinguishing between acts before and after the 'Asr prayer. Imam al-Baqir (AS) prescribes a single make-up day for pre-'Asr acts, but requires fasting the day, feeding ten poor, or fasting three days for post-'Asr acts. The narration concludes with Muhammad ibn al-Hasan resolving apparent contradictions by interpreting the rulings as obligatory in one context and recommended in another, reflecting the nuanced Shia jurisprudential approach to time-based legal distinctions.
